structured_output.what_is_happening: Metsumi404 is a "404"-style token with a fixed supply of about 4,444 tokens (price about $24, mcap about $107k). Its pitch is "burn one token to hardwire one terminal". It launched about 18:10 UTC on a Meteora virtual curve, migrated within about 2 minutes and trades on several pairs; the tracked one is a Meteora DLMM pool with about $8k liquidity. It hit an ATH price of about $106.8 (about $470k mcap) and is now about 77% below it. The last hour shows -57% to -62%, and the trigger fired during a volatile bounce (m5 was -25% at detection, +6% to +26% at collection). Nearly all volume ($62k) came in the last hour. A second 'Metsumi404' contract (3f7fo…), created about 50 minutes later, is doing $913k of h1 volume on $35k liquidity at about $137k mcap. It is taking far more attention than this contract. Many other zero-liquidity copies exist.

narrative.description: This is a revival of the ERC-404 / hybrid token-NFT gimmick: a tiny fixed supply of 4,444, with burning a token to 'hardwire a terminal'. The theme is aesthetic and cyberpunk, and it has a website plus an X account. The concept is novel enough to draw a quick wave of degen attention, but most of that attention now appears to have moved to a competing contract.
narrative.why_spreading: The 404 mechanic plus the tiny supply give a high unit price, which gets curiosity trades. 36 smart and 6 renowned wallets touched it. But the price has already fallen 77% from ATH, and flow is shifting to another same-name contract.

token_connection.why_this_token: This contract was created first (18:10) and carries the DexScreener profile, the website metsumi.cash and the X handle Metsumi404. That points to it being the original deployment.
token_connection.competing_tokens: 3f7fo… 'Metsumi404' was created about 50 minutes later. It has $913k h1 volume versus this contract's $62k and 3-4x the liquidity, so it looks like either a relaunch or migration by the team or a hijack that won the flow. There are about 8 other zero-liquidity clones, plus older unrelated 'Metsumi' tokens.

authenticity.evidence: There are 174 bundler-tagged wallets out of 550, a bot/degen rate of 55% and 357 fresh wallets. The dev's X account has launched 15 tokens. On the other side, the holder spread is reasonable (top10 about 24%), the dev holds 0%, there is no paid promotion, and 36 smart and 6 renowned wallets participated. The buyer and seller counts are close to even (275/276), which fits rotation or churn.
authenticity.uncertainty: There is no X data, so I can't tell whether the team endorsed the second contract (which would make this one abandoned) or whether that one is a hijack.

structural_risks: The tracked DLMM pool has only about $8k liquidity; DLMM positions can be withdrawn
The price is 77% below ATH and the downtrend has been sharp in the last hour
Attention and volume have moved to a competing same-name contract with 15x the volume
174 bundler wallets and heavy bot share
The dev's X account has launched 15 tokens

structured_output.counterargument: This could be the canonical original. If the team or the community rejects the 3f7fo contract as a copy, flow could rotate back here. A 2x only needs a return to about $50 (about $215k mcap), still less than half the ATH, and 404 gimmicks with tiny supply can swing hard on thin liquidity. The smart and renowned wallet presence also suggests real interest.

structured_output.thesis: This is a post-peak coin about 77% below ATH. It has been outcompeted by a same-name contract doing 15x its volume, and it has thin DLMM liquidity plus heavy bundler and bot participation. A 2x within 6 hours would need flow to rotate back decisively, which is unlikely. The more probable outcomes are a slow bleed or death.
